title: NA-Aware Defaults for Common R Functions
text: Summary: mean, weighted.mean, sum, prod, sd, var, median, quantile Extrema: min, max, pmin, pmax, range Logical: , Row-wise: rowSums, rowMeans Correlation: cor Table: table

title: NA-Aware Defaults for Common R Functions
text: -NA input configurable: default, tidyna throws error values NA prevent misleading values like Inf, NaN, 0: can change behavior all_na argument tidyna.all_na option: rowSums/rowMeans return NA -NA rows, error entire matrix NA. Also configurable via all_na. pmax/pmin return NA positions inputs NA (warning), error every position -NA. Also configurable via all_na. cor defaults use = "pairwise.complete.obs" instead erroring NAs. table defaults useNA = "ifany", showing NA counts present rather silently dropping .
code: base::sum(c(NA, NA), na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 0  sum(c(NA, NA)) #> Error in `sum()`: #> ! All values are NA; check if something went wrong. # Return base R behavior (NaN, Inf, 0, etc.) sum(c(NA, NA), all_na = "base") #> [1] 0  # Always return NA sum(c(NA, NA), all_na = "na") #> [1] NA

title: NA-Aware Defaults for Common R Functions
text: free lunch. tidyna package adds overhead:  functions like mean() overhead negligible (1.1x). rowMeans() rowSums() require extra pass detect -NA rows, substantial loss (3-4x). ’m still working whether memory allocation needs addressed.

title: NA-aware Extrema Functions — extrema-functions

title: NA-aware Extrema Functions — extrema-functions
code: min(..., na.rm = TRUE, all_na = NULL)  max(..., na.rm = TRUE, all_na = NULL)  range(..., na.rm = TRUE, all_na = NULL, finite = FALSE)  pmax(..., na.rm = TRUE, all_na = NULL)  pmin(..., na.rm = TRUE, all_na = NULL)

title: NA-aware Extrema Functions — extrema-functions
text: ... Numeric character arguments. na.rm Logical. missing values removed? Default TRUE. all_na Character. values NA: "error" (default) throws error, "base" returns base R na.rm = TRUE (e.g., Inf min(), -Inf max()), "na" returns NA. NULL, uses getOption("tidyna.all_na", "error"). finite Logical. TRUE, removes non-finite values (NA, NaN, Inf, -Inf). applies range(). Default FALSE.

title: NA-aware Extrema Functions — extrema-functions
text: min() max(), length-one vector. range(), length-two vector containing minimum maximum. pmax() pmin(), vector length equal longest input.

title: NA-aware Extrema Functions — extrema-functions
code: x <- c(1, NA, 5, 3) min(x) #> Warning: ⚠️ 1 missing value removed. #> [1] 1 max(x) #> Warning: ⚠️ 1 missing value removed. #> [1] 5 range(x) #> Warning: ⚠️ 1 missing value removed. #> [1] 1 5  # Multiple arguments min(c(5, NA), c(1, 2)) #> Warning: ⚠️ 1 missing value removed. #> [1] 1  # Parallel max/min pmax(c(1, 5, 3), c(2, 1, 4)) #> [1] 2 5 4 pmin(c(1, NA, 3), c(NA, NA, 1)) #> Warning: ⚠️ 1 missing value removed. #> Warning: ⚠️ 1 position had all NA values. #> [1]  1 NA  1  # range with infinite values y <- c(1, Inf, 3, -Inf) range(y) #> [1] -Inf  Inf range(y, finite = TRUE) #> Warning: ⚠️ 2 infinite values removed. #> [1] 1 3

title: tidyna: NA-Aware Defaults for Common R Functions — tidyna-package
text: Provides drop-replacements common R functions (mean(), sum(), sd(), min(), etc.) default 'na.rm = TRUE' issue warnings missing values removed. handles special cases. table() default set 'useNA = ifany'.

title: tidyna: NA-Aware Defaults for Common R Functions — tidyna-package
text: attach tidyna library(tidyna), masks base/stats functions: mean, sum, prod (base) min, max, range, pmax, pmin (base) , (base) sd, var, median, quantile (stats) rowMeans, rowSums (base) cor (stats) table (base)

title: tidyna: NA-Aware Defaults for Common R Functions — tidyna-package
text: tidyna.warn: Set FALSE suppress warnings. Default TRUE. tidyna.all_na: Controls behavior values NA. One "error" (default, throws error), "base" (returns base R behavior), "na" (returns NA).

title: tidyna 0.5.0
text: weighted.mean() now defaults na.rm = TRUE warns missing values removed. Unlike base R, missing values either x w cause corresponding pair dropped.

title: tidyna 0.4.1
text: quantile() now works without naming probs argument, e.g., quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)).

title: tidyna 0.4.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-01-27 functions now support configurable -NA behavior via all_na argument. Choose "error" (default, current behavior), "base" (return base R values like NaN, Inf, 0 depending function), "na" (always return NA). Set globally options(tidyna.all_na = "base").

title: tidyna 0.3.0
text: pmax() pmin() now default na.rm = TRUE warn NAs removed. Positions inputs NA return NA warning. -NAs every position yields error.

title: tidyna 0.2.0
text: range() now defaults na.rm = TRUE warns NAs removed. Supports finite argument also remove infinite values warning.

title: tidyna 0.1.3
text: Small QoL changes.
